decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall be begun within 3 years from the date of this permission.

Reason: To accord with the provisions of Section 92 (1) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Condition : 2 - The proposed development shall be carried out in all respects in accordance with the proposals contained in the application and the plans submitted (Design and access statement, fire safety strategy, biodiversity net gain, BNG metric, AR-P01, AR-P02, planning statement, summary energy statement

Received: 09/07/2025

Full SAP calcs 

Received: 22/09/2025

AR-P03, AR-P04, AR-P05, AR-P06, AR-P07

Received: 31/10/2025

Drainage Assessment Form

Received: 07/11/2025) 

therewith and approved by the Local Planning Authority, or as shall have been otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority before the building is used.

Reason: To ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission.

Condition : 3 - The materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted shall match those shown on the approved plans. 

Reason: In order to safeguard the appearance of the area

Condition : 4 - A)	The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy.

B)	Prior to first occupation of the development hereby approved, the relevant carbon offset payment shall have been made and evidence (e.g. photographs, installation contracts and As-Built certificates under the Standard Assessment Procedure/National Calculation Method) shall be submitted to the local planning authority and approved in writing to show that the development has been constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy, and any subsequent approved revisions, and achieved a 80% reduction in emissions. 

Reason: In order to ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions.

Condition : 5 - The development shall have been constructed to achieve an internal water use of 105 litres/person/day or less.

Reason: In order to protect and conserve water supplies and resources.

Condition : 6 - Notwithstanding the submitted details and prior to occupation, full details of hard and soft landscaping shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details as approved, shall be implemented prior to first occupation of the new dwelling and shall thereafter be retained as such.
These details shall include
(a) Hard and soft landscaping (including materials) 
(b) Boundary treatments 
Reason: In order to ensure a satisfactory appearance of the site and the area and to promote biodiversity.

Condition : 7 - Notwithstanding the submitted details and prior to occupation, full details (including manufacturer's specifications) of all cycle stands for the occupants of the development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved facilities shall be fully implemented and made available for use before any part of the development is first occupied and thereafter retained for use at all times without obstruction. 

Reason: In order to support sustainable transport objectives.

Condition : 8 - Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development Order) 1995 (or any order revoking or re-enacting that order), no enlargement of the premises or any additional structures/buildings/enclosures within the curtilage of the site shall be carried out, other than as shown in the approved drawings, and no additional floor space shall be formed within the building(s) hereby permitted by means of internal horizontal division (new mezzanine level) without prior written approval of the local planning authority.
Reason: To protect neighbours' living conditions

Condition : 9 - Prior to the first commencement of the hereby approved development, a Biodiversity Gain Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, the Plan shall include; 
(a) information about the steps taken or to be taken to minimise the adverse effect of the development on the biodiversity of the onsite habitat and any other habitat, 
(b) the pre-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat, 
(c) the post-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat, 
(d) any registered offsite biodiversity gain allocated to the development and the biodiversity value of that gain in relation to the development, 
(e) any biodiversity credits purchased for the development, and 
(f) such other matters as the Secretary of State may by regulations specify. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Plan prior to the first occupation of the development. Any habitats created or enhanced on-site and off-site in accordance with the Biodiversity Gain Plan must be maintained thereafter for a minimum of 30 years. 
Reason. In the interests of improving Biodiversity and in accordance with The Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Section 90A, Schedule 7A.

Condition : 10 - Prior to commencement of groundworks (excluding site investigations and demolition), the applicant must submit a final detailed drainage design including drawings and detailed supporting calculations [and updated Drainage Assessment Form] to the Lead Local Flood Authority for review and approval, aligned with the [Drainage Documentation (11/11/2025)] and associated drawings, including rainwater harvesting. Evidence of infiltration testing which demonstrates suitable infiltration rates is required. A detailed management plan confirming routine maintenance tasks for all drainage components must also be submitted to demonstrate how the drainage system is to be maintained for the lifetime of the development. A maintenance owner should be provided.

Reason: To prevent the risk of flooding to and from the site

Condition : 11 - No building hereby permitted shall be occupied until evidence (photographs and installation contracts) is submitted to demonstrate that the sustainable drainage scheme for the site has been completed in accordance with the submitted details. The sustainable drainage scheme shall be managed and maintained thereafter in accordance with the agreed management and maintenance plan for all of the proposed drainage components.

Reason: To comply with the Non-Statutory Technical Standards for Sustainable Drainage Systems

Condition : 12 - Before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, the existing vehicular access to Trevithick Close shall be permanently closed and kerbs/verge/footway reinstated so that it cannot be used as an access across the pavement.

Reason: In order to enhance the pedestrian environment and to confine vehicular access to the permitted points in order to ensure that the development does not prejudice the free flow of traffic or highway safety along the adjacent highway.
